title: Tentative Output Orchestrator: routing policy, early-accept scoring, and fallback runbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a Tentative Output Orchestrator (TOO) that manages routing decisions for speculative decoding flows, evaluates early-accept scores from partial-prefill outputs, and executes a robust fallback runbook when optimistic paths underperform. This ticket covers the runtime decision policy, integration points for kernel affinity signals, attention-optimization hints, telemetry contracts, and the operational fallback playbook for degraded modes.
background: We have multiple optimistic execution patterns in the runtime that attempt early token commits from faster model variants or cached prefill fragments. Current implementations lack a centralized decision layer that reasons about kernel fit, attention profile heuristics, and confidence-to-cost tradeoffs. This leads to suboptimal fallbacks (full decode restarts, excess compute), unclear telemetry for acceptance quality, and ad-hoc rollback behaviour across services.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight orchestrator module that sits between the scheduler and decode engine. Responsibilities: 1) collect per-candidate signals (kernel_score, attention_span_estimate, kv_cache_match_ratio, latency_budget_remaining); 2) compute an early-accept score using a calibrated logistic model; 3) choose whether to commit an optimistic token path or continue conservative decode; 4) if early-accept fails, run a staged fallback: merge KV caches when possible, resume conservative decode from last safe boundary, chargeback metrics, and emit a detailed incident record.
design_decisions: Use a deterministic scoring function (configurable weights) as primary decision path; ML-based scorer can be toggled for experiments.
Expose kernel affinity as a numeric signal (0..1) derived from kernel fingerprint match and micro-benchmark lookup.
Treat attention profile hints (locality, windowed attention) as modifiers to expected per-token cost and adjust acceptance threshold accordingly.
Fallback must prefer incremental recovery (resume conservative decode) over full request restart where KV cache interoperability exists.
Make scoring function explainable and log feature contributions for post-hoc evals and SLIs.
acceptance_criteria: TOO returns deterministic decision within 150us p95 for typical candidate set sizes (<=3 candidates)
Early-accept decisions reduce end-to-end median latency by >=7% on workloads with >30% cache hits and maintain token-level quality delta <0.8 BLEU-equivalent metric against conservative baseline
When a fallback occurs, total extra compute (GPU ms) must be <1.5x of a single conservative decode for the same request in 95% of cases
Telemetry emitted for every decision: candidate_signals, score, decision, fallback_reason (if any), latency_ms, commit_boundary
Feature-gated rollout path and unit/integration tests for kernel affinity input, attention modifiers, and fallback behaviour exist in the runtime repo
tasks: Spec: formalize scoring schema and canonical signal names (ENG PRD link)
Runtime: implement TOO module with pluggable scorer interface
Scheduler: add hooks to attach kernel affinity and attention hints to candidate tokens
KV layer: expose mergeable cache API to support incremental fallback resumes
Telemetry: add decision tracer and event schema to Console ingestion pipeline
E2E tests: synthetic workloads (high/low cache, narrow/wide attention) and perf baselines
Docs: document config knobs, thresholds, and runbook in runbooks/confluence
Postmortem playbook: template for recording fallback incidents and customer-visible impact

telemetry_metrics: too.feature_contrib.<feature_name> (logged as histogram for post-hoc calibration)
rollout_plan: Alpha: gated flag in runtime on non-prod clusters; observational only (no commit) for 2 weeks
Beta: enable commit for <internal-team> traffic with conservative thresholds for 1 week; monitor too.fallback.extra_gpu_ms and user-visible latency
Gradual: increase to 10% of hosted API traffic, then 50% over a month if quality and SLOs hold
Rollback: global kill switch and per-region knob; automated rollback if fallback.extra_gpu_ms.p95 > 2x baseline or user-error-rate increases >0.5%
Post-rollout: schedule model-eval to compare output quality across 24h sample and produce release note
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect scoring weights cause higher degrade rates. Mitigation: conservative defaults + canary with traffic split + feature-flagged ML scorer
Risk: KV cache incompatibility leads to expensive restarts. Mitigation: require cache merge contract in KV API before enabling commit; fallback always prefers resume when mergeable
Risk: Telemetry volume increases. Mitigation: sample event payloads and emit full traces only on fallback events
Risk: Per-decision latency regresses SLO. Mitigation: decision path bounded (150us) and fast-path optimizations (precomputed kernel affinity)
